na_rules.reason: Temporal contrast queries require a temporal graph class: a pulse, sustained, temporal-conditional or temporal-mediation contrast is indexed by a lag and a horizon, and a static graph class has no time index for either.

Static queries do not denote on TemporalDag, TemporalCpdag, or TemporalPag. TemporalPag stays the equivalence class only for the temporal queries licensed on it. Latent confounding over time denotes on TemporalAdmg. An AverageEffect on a temporal graph denotes the lag-0 contrast and is a refused, executing cell (parity/support_closed.toml).
TransportQuery and InterferenceQuery are typed against static graphs; they do not denote on a temporal graph class.
cheap and full denote the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; a function-valued curve has no such state.
cheap and full denote the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; a graph-posterior response remains function-valued or atom-mixed with no licensed scalar-refuter state.
Unknown-tier cells license the two-scenario AverageEffect envelope only.
CoDetermined cells license AverageEffect and joint InterventionResponse only.
Tier-rule backgrounds are an explicit structure source.
cheap and full name the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; CoDetermined joint IR and the Unknown envelope have no licensed scalar-refuter state.

closed_rules.reason: A path-restricted natural effect or an interventional distribution over a graph posterior is answered on every atom by the executor the query has on a supplied structure of the atom's kind: the path-specific identifier and finite-discrete functional plug-in on a DAG or an ADMG (the contemporaneous projection for a TemporalAdmg atom), and the completion envelope on a CPDAG (every DAG completion) or a PAG (every ADMG sharing the m-separation model of a MAG completion). The atoms mix by posterior probability: the effect is the posterior-weighted mean over the atoms that identify and evaluate it, an interventional distribution is the posterior-weighted mean probability of each outcome level (an atom lacking a level has probability zero there) with the mean beside it, and an atom whose class publishes an identified set contributes its range to the mixture's identified set. An atom the identifier refuses (a recanting district, a hedge, a class every member of which refuses) is unidentified posterior mass and an atom whose plug-in cannot be evaluated is unevaluable mass; neither is redistributed, the result states both and resolves its status to graph-dependent when either exceeds the tolerance. The uncertainty of a mixture: one contributing atom carries its own interval and posterior; several atoms are re-run on shared resampled tables and the standard error is the spread of the draw-wise posterior-weighted mixture (Frequentist), or their draws are pooled draw by draw because every atom runs in one context (Bayesian); an interval that cannot be formed is withheld with the reason stated (estimate.graph_posterior.cross_world_uncertainty). A mixed graph or a class reads an unconditional finite-discrete table. Cheap and full run each atom's own refuter suite against that atom's own estimate and mix the reports of each refuter by the posterior weight of the atoms that produced them; a mixed verdict passes only if every contributing atom passes, and a refuter that ran on only part of the contributing mass says so (refute.envelope.partial_coverage). The result keeps support status refused; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

A MediationEffect over a graph posterior decomposes the effect into its total, natural direct and natural indirect components on every atom with the executor the query has on a supplied structure of the atom's kind (the Dag cell's own estimator on a DAG, the path-specific identifier and finite-discrete plug-in on an ADMG or a TemporalAdmg atom's contemporaneous projection, the completion envelope on a CPDAG or a PAG), and mixes each component by posterior probability over the atoms that identify it. A component the identifier refuses on an atom (a recanting district for the pure natural indirect effect) is that component's unidentified mass only and is never imputed as total minus direct; a component no atom identifies is reported absent; the requested contrast must be identified by at least one atom. An atom the identifier refuses for the requested contrast is unidentified posterior mass and an atom whose plug-in cannot be evaluated is unevaluable mass, neither redistributed, and the status resolves to graph-dependent when either exceeds the tolerance. The uncertainty of a mixture: one contributing atom carries its own interval and posterior; several atoms are re-run on shared resampled tables and the standard error is the spread of the draw-wise posterior-weighted mixture (Frequentist), or their draws are pooled draw by draw because every atom runs in one context (Bayesian); an interval that cannot be formed is withheld with the reason stated (estimate.graph_posterior.cross_world_uncertainty). Cheap and full run each atom's own refuter suite against that atom's own estimate and mix the reports of each refuter by the posterior weight of the atoms that produced them; a mixed verdict passes only if every contributing atom passes, and a refuter that ran on only part of the contributing mass says so (refute.envelope.partial_coverage). The result keeps support status refused; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

Cheap and full validation of a change attribution on a supplied or accepted Cpdag, Pag, Admg, TemporalAdmg, TemporalCpdag or TemporalPag is refused. The validation would refit the vector of total change and component contributions on random row subsets and on bootstrap resamples drawn within each of the two populations, and report one joint chi-square statistic against the original. The total change is a difference of two population means and the allocation a Shapley function of mechanism swaps, so a within-population subset or resample leaves the replicate mean at the original whatever heterogeneity is planted: the same derivation holds for every member of a class and every atom of a posterior, which are each attributed by the DAG or noise-block route whose replicates are such subsets and resamples. A verdict that cannot tell a sound attribution from an unsound one is not evidence, so the cell refuses instead of reporting one. Next attempt: a planted-violation design for the allocation (a mechanism that differs between the halves of one population), checked against an exact reference.

Cheap and full validation of an interventional distribution on an Admg or TemporalAdmg run the functional refuter state and stay unlicensed. The identified functional executes as at validation none; the vector of atom probabilities is refitted by the same compiled program on random row subsets and, under full, on bootstrap resamples (circular blocks on a TemporalAdmg), each refuter a joint chi-square statistic over the atoms. The atoms are levels of a law, so the treatment-keyed null refuters do not apply. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell, and the verdicts are diagnostics, not a calibration claim.

Natural mediation on one series under a TemporalPag is identified on the finite window of its template, as a pulse contrast is: the treatment is the pulse period's coordinate, the outcome the horizon period's coordinate, and the mediators are the declared mediator variables at every period from the pulse to the outcome. Each stationary MAG completion of the template is unfolded over the window one template lag further back and marginalized onto it by the inducing-path rule, so a cause that precedes the window stays a bidirected edge between its in-window effects, and is then read through every ADMG that shares the marginal MAG, because a MAG fixes a latent projection only up to its m-separation model and a path-specific effect is not a function of that model. The path-specific identifier decides the total, natural direct and natural indirect effects on each candidate (the edge g-formula, or Shpitser's district formula with the recanting-district criterion); the requested contrast is reported only when every candidate of every completion identifies it, as one estimate when they yield the same functional and as the identified set over the distinct functionals otherwise, and a refused candidate refuses the effect. A component other than the requested one that the identifier refuses is reported absent. The decomposition is estimated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table with circular blocks of consecutive windows (frequentist) or one Dirichlet weight per block (Bayesian), the components on the same resampled tables when each is identified by one functional, and the result discloses estimate.mediation.joint and estimate.temporal_pag.window. The series is read as stationary over the template, and history deeper than one further template lag is the initial state. One outcome horizon per study; discrete data only. Cheap and full run the mediation-native suite on the window table (sequential-ignorability sensitivity of the indirect effect, a mediator placebo that rotates the mediator columns by whole windows, and the joint stability of the three components on contiguous stretches of windows and, under full, 50% stretches and a joint block bootstrap range); when the completions identify different functionals the suite runs on every distinct member. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

A counterfactual over a graph posterior of PAG atoms under cheap or full validation is refused, as on a supplied PAG. The effect on the treated is identified only through a visible treatment edge, so the treatment has an observed parent whose association with the outcome runs through the treatment; the placebo treatment permutes the treatment and leaves that association on the outcome with no mechanism to carry it, so its statistic is nonzero on a correctly specified design and the refuter state would flag valid data. Next attempt: a placebo that permutes the treatment within the strata of its parents and re-derives the outcome part the treatment carries, then earn it with a planted-violation and a clean-case test.

A graph posterior over TemporalPag atoms mixes the mediation decomposition over the atoms: each atom is a stationary template read as a supplied TemporalPag is (unfolded over the window of the pulse and its outcome horizon, every stationary MAG completion marginalized onto it and read through the ADMGs that share its MAG, the decomposition identified only when every candidate of every completion identifies the requested contrast, and evaluated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table with circular blocks of consecutive windows or one Dirichlet weight per block), and the components are mixed by posterior probability, each over the atoms that identify it. An atom whose window leaves the requested contrast unidentified keeps its mass as unidentified mass, an atom whose plug-in cannot be evaluated is unevaluable mass, and an atom whose completions identify different functionals publishes its identified set, the union of which is the mixture's identified set beside the posterior-weighted point; neither lost mass is redistributed. The uncertainty of a mixture: one contributing atom carries its own interval and posterior; several atoms are re-run on shared resampled series (circular blocks of consecutive periods, no shorter than the window) and the standard error is the spread of the draw-wise posterior-weighted mixture (Frequentist), or their draws are pooled draw by draw because every atom runs in one context (Bayesian) (estimate.graph_posterior.cross_world_uncertainty). One outcome horizon per study; discrete data only. Cheap and full run each atom's own refuter suite against that atom's own estimate and mix the reports of each refuter by the posterior weight of the atoms that produced them; a mixed verdict passes only if every contributing atom passes, and a refuter that ran on only part of the contributing mass says so (refute.envelope.partial_coverage). The result keeps support status refused; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

Cheap and full validation of an interventional distribution on a supplied or accepted Cpdag, Pag, Admg or TemporalAdmg run the functional refuter state and stay unlicensed. The identified functional executes as at validation none (in every completion of a class); a path-specific effect is refuted by the placebo treatment, subset stability and, under full, the placebo outcome and bootstrap stability of the whole procedure, and an interventional distribution by subset and bootstrap stability of its vector of atom probabilities, each a joint statistic over the whole refitted value. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell, and the verdicts are diagnostics, not a calibration claim.

A pulse, sustained or conditional contrast on one series under a TemporalAdmg is identified on the unrolled window of its template: the template is unrolled over the periods the policy needs (a cause that precedes the window is a latent common cause of its in-window effects), the complete ID algorithm identifies both sides of the contrast (IDC with the modifiers read at the first treated period for a conditional contrast), and the identified functional is evaluated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table. Frequentist uncertainty resamples circular blocks of consecutive windows and Bayesian uncertainty shares one Dirichlet weight per block, never shorter than the window, because overlapping windows invalidate a row-level draw; the series is read as stationary over the template. Cheap validation refits the plug-in on a random contiguous stretch of 80% of the windows and rotates the treatment columns together by at least one window, which must give a contrast indistinguishable from zero; full validation adds a 50% stretch and a split-half stationarity test (the contrast on the first half of the windows against the second, each with a circular-block bootstrap standard error). Both inference modes run the same window-native suite on the plug-in. The result keeps support status refused and discloses estimate.temporal_admg.window; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell. A window that holds a hedge is refused with the variables and periods that carry it, and a modifier a treated period can reach is refused. Discrete data only.

A graph posterior over lagged TemporalAdmg atoms mixes the window contrast of the rule above over the posterior: an atom is a stationary template (a contemporaneous ADMG, lagged directed edges and lagged latent-confounder edges), the contrast is identified on the unrolled window of each atom's own template, the identified functional of each atom is evaluated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table of its window length (atoms with different lags read tables of different lengths), and the atoms are mixed by posterior weight. An atom whose window holds a hedge, or whose modifier a treated period can reach, keeps its mass as unidentified mass and the mixture is then graph-dependent rather than a point. Frequentist uncertainty of one atom resamples circular blocks of consecutive windows; the standard error of a mixture of several atoms is the spread of the draw-wise mixture of their replicates at the same resampled table (atoms that read tables of different lengths publish no mixture standard error). Bayesian atoms share one Dirichlet weight per block and the aggregate posterior of a mixture of several atoms is withheld, as for a static ADMG posterior. The result keeps support status refused and discloses estimate.graph_posterior.temporal_admg_window; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell. Posteriors over contemporaneous TemporalAdmg atoms (no lag masks) read tabular rows and have no window. Cheap and full validation run the window-native suite (stretch refits, the rotated-treatment placebo and, under full, 50% stretches and the split-half stationarity test) on every atom that carries posterior weight, each on the window table of its own template, and mix the per-atom reports by posterior weight: the mixed check passes only when every contributing atom passed.

Natural mediation on one series under a TemporalAdmg is identified on the unrolled window of its template, as a pulse contrast is: the treatment is the pulse period's coordinate, the outcome the horizon period's coordinate, and the mediators are the declared mediator variables at every period from the pulse to the outcome. The path-specific identifier decides the total, natural direct and natural indirect effects on that window ADMG (the edge g-formula, or Shpitser's district formula with the recanting-district criterion), and a cause that precedes the window is a latent common cause of its in-window effects. The decomposition is estimated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table with circular blocks of consecutive windows (frequentist) or one Dirichlet weight per block (Bayesian), the components on the same resampled tables, and the result discloses estimate.mediation.joint and estimate.temporal_admg.window. The requested contrast must be identified; a component the identifier refuses is reported absent. Cheap and full run the mediation-native suite on the window table (sequential-ignorability sensitivity of the indirect effect, a mediator placebo that rotates the mediator columns by whole windows, and the joint stability of the three components on contiguous stretches of windows and, under full, 50% stretches and a joint block bootstrap range). One outcome horizon per study; discrete data only. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

A graph posterior over lagged TemporalAdmg atoms mixes the mediation decomposition of the rule above over the posterior: each atom (a stationary template with lagged directed and lagged latent-confounder edges) decomposes into the total, natural direct and natural indirect effects on the unrolled window of its own template by the path-specific identifier, each component is evaluated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table of the atom's window length, and the atoms that identify a component are mixed by posterior weight for that component. An atom that leaves the requested contrast unidentified (a recanting district, a hedge) keeps its mass as unidentified mass and the mixture is graph-dependent; a component other than the requested one is mixed over the atoms that identify it and reported absent when none does. Uncertainty is that of the supplied-template window route (circular blocks of consecutive windows, or one Dirichlet weight per block), and the aggregate posterior of a mixture of several atoms is withheld. One outcome horizon per study; discrete data only. Cheap and full run the mediation-native suite on every atom that carries posterior weight (all three components of the atom refitted together on the window table of its own template) and mix the per-atom reports by posterior weight: the mixed check passes only when every contributing atom passed. The result keeps support status refused and discloses estimate.graph_posterior.temporal_admg_window.

A natural direct effect over a graph posterior of Dag atoms is refused under full validation. The full suite runs the Dag-native refuters on every atom, which need linear-Gaussian mechanism families a discrete atom table does not have, so every atom fails and the failure would read as non-identification. Next attempt: answer the full suite of a Dag atom through the functional refuter state, as the ADMG atoms are, then earn it with the atom-mixture fixture.
